memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: ""We must take a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the Lord our God, as he commands us." Pharaoh said, "I will let you go to offer sacrifices to the Lord your God in the wilderness, but you must not go very far. Now pray for me."" - Exodus 8:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh's second compromise is subtler than the first. Fine — go. But do not go very far.

That is a shrewd tactic. If they stay close, they can be pulled back. Distance from Egypt was exactly what Israel needed.

Spiritually, this is a strategy we should recognise. The temptation is rarely to abandon our faith outright; it is to stay close enough to our old life that returning is easy. Keep the number saved. Keep the app installed. Keep the friendship that always pulls you down. Do not go very far.

Scripture speaks more decisively. Joseph ran from temptation. Paul told Timothy to flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness (2 Tim 2:22). Sometimes the only safe distance is a long one.

And notice Pharaoh's last three words: now pray for me. Even while manipulating, he still wants the benefit of prayer. Some people want God's help without God's rule.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have I kept close "just in case", that I should put real distance between myself and?
2. Am I asking God for help while resisting His authority?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me courage to go far from what harms me. I want Your rule, not only Your help. Amen.
